subject: Lattice Health - SLO kickoff & ops handoff (throughput/latency constraints)
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Ana Morales <ana.morales@latticehealth.com>, Devin Park <devin.park@latticehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Lattice Health - SLO kickoff & ops handoff (throughput/latency constraints)

Thanks Ana and Devin — good conversation this morning. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps from the call. I’ve summarized the pain, the target SLOs, and recommended immediate actions below.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Inference cost and burst behavior causing unpredictable spend near peak business hours.
- p99 spikes during short bursts of heavy traffic that break downstream UX SLAs.
- Concern about model drift and rollout risk when we scale to production.

Goals we discussed (what success looks like):
- Stable p95 latency <= 120 ms for single-turn text completions at typical request sizes (avg 512 tokens).
- p99 tail below 350 ms for 95% of steady-state traffic; acceptable degradation windows during sustained bursts with graceful fallback.
- Predictable throughput: baseline 25-30 qps with headroom for 2–3x bursts during peak.
- Data residency in US-only region for PHI pipeline; audit logging retained for 90 days.

Technical constraints / model requirements you called out:
- Primary model: OpenModelX-34B (quantized variant acceptable for cost) for most traffic; smaller ensemble for fallback (7B quant).
- Many requests are short (single-turn), but several routes include long-context prompts (~2k tokens) for triage workflows.
- Platform must support KV-cache-friendly routing and prefix caching for repeated conversation prefixes.

Recommended topology (short):
- Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) in us-east with autoscaling policy defined by queue depth + token rate.
- Canary route to a quantized 7B variant for fallbacks with automatic traffic-shift policy on latency breach.
- Prefix/KV cache enabled at the routing layer with 60s TTL for hot keys, backed by warm-up preloads for high-frequency flows.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
1) We (Redwood) will send a deployment sketch (MOP diagram) and a first-pass autoscaling policy for your infra — see attached MOP-Deployment-Diagram.png.
2) Lattice to share a small sample of request logs (anonymized) and a couple of representative payloads so we can run a targeted latency profile. Recommended format: JSONL with timestamps, token counts, and response sizes (sample schema attached in this thread).
3) Kimberly (solutions engineer) will propose a canary run plan and success criteria for an initial 3-week POC.
4) Procurement timeline: Ana said procurement targets signing a terms addendum within 6 weeks.

Deliverables / timings:
- MOP diagram + autoscale suggestion (Redwood) — EOD Friday (2027-04-16).
- Platform sample-run results (Redwood) after logs received — ~3 business days.
- POC kickoff call (we suggested week of 4/26) — confirm availability.

If any of the above is off in your view, call it out and I’ll update. Devin — can you share the anonymized logs and one example full payload (no PHI) by end of day Friday?

Thanks,

Markus Klein

- The p95 target of <=120ms is for our UI-facing endpoints (most requests are ~200–600 tokens). For our triage/analytics batch jobs (longer prompts) we’re ok with higher latency if throughput is predictable.
- Procurement: we do intend to move quickly but need legal to sign the standard DPA + addendum; target still ~6 weeks but could slip to 8.

Devin — I’ll leave the logs task to you. We will strip PHI and any patient identifiers. Hi Ana/Devin — looping in a short technical readout based on the sample logs attached and our prior experience with similar PHI pipelines. I focused on the parts that will affect the deployment sketch and POC sizing.

Quick technical notes from our side:
- Baseline sizing: to hit 25–30 qps with avg 512 tokens and p95 <=120 ms we expect a pool roughly equivalent to 4x A100-style workers (quantized paths) or 6x T4-style scaled workers depending on model variant. We’ll size the POC conservatively and then tune.
- Fallbacks: recommend an automated fast-fail route to a quantized 7B model when queue depth or observed p99 exceeds threshold for >30s. That preserves UX while we degrade quality gracefully.
- Caching: enable prefix caching at the edge with a 60s TTL for high-frequency query signatures; consider warm-up preloads for known heavy endpoints at POC start.
- Canaries & rollouts: canary traffic should be limited to 5–10% for 24h with realtime latency/quality monitoring. If latency breach occurs, automatic rollback to the baseline model variant.
- Metrics we need for the POC: request_size_tokens, model_variant, enqueue_time, dequeue_time, serve_lat_ms, response_token_count. The sample JSONL you sent looks good — thanks.

Cost guidance (very rough):
- Dedicated reserved pool (3-week POC): estimated incremental cost ~ 1.8x hosted burst for sustained baseline, but with much lower variance and predictable tail behavior.
- Hosted burst/as-needed: cheaper on average if traffic is spiky and short-lived, but exposes you to p99 tail variance and cold-start penalties.

Action items for Lattice (from the call and sample review):
1) Confirm which routes are UI-critical (require p95 120ms) vs analytic (throughput-first). A mapping table is enough.
2) Share any SLO budgets per route (error budget/acceptable downtime windows).
3) Give us access to the staging bucket or drop 1–2 large representative payloads so we can run end-to-end latency tests (tokenization + decode).

I’ll put together the detailed canary plan and the autoscale policy draft by Monday. Markus — feel free to add timing.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
